article.title: Cuba Needs Medicine
article.author: Mark Friedman
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Support for Cuba in its fight against the criminal economic, commercial, financial and energy blockade imposed by the United States was the focus of one of the workshops held at the annual "Left Coast Forum" at California State University in Los Angeles, from October 2 to 4. In that solidarity space, they discussed how to materialize more donations to Cuba as a way to challenge the unilateral coercive measures of the White House, based on a campaign promoted by the organization Global Health Partners and the "Hands-Off Cuba" Committee. Related: Using Olympics as Weapon Against Cuban People He was updated on the recent measures imposed by the Donald Trump administration with the signing of two presidential decrees in 2026, plus the inclusion of Cuba in the unilateral and spurious list of state sponsors of terrorism, which intensify the sanctions already imposed previously. Union leader Mark Friedman, a member of the International Machinists' Association (IAM) No. 1484 and the Los Angeles "Hands Off Cuba" Committee, commented that several speakers alluded to the importance of delivering medicines and solar technology to the Caribbean Island to contribute to the energy matrix change. They referred to the Cuban people's resilience in the face of the harsh measures taken by the far-right Trump administration, which have prevented fuel shipments for more than ten months. They also referred to the warmongering threats of invasion and the pressure exerted from hegemonic positions to achieve a change of political power in Cuba, something inconceivable to the Cuban people, as Mark Friedman explained. Furthermore, they gave examples of recent trips by Americans where they verified the Cuban reality and contrasted it with the media campaigns promoted by traditional media and social networks, in an attempt to discredit the Cuban political process. Cuba Needs Medicine and Energy, Not More U.S. Sanctions (52:26) The event addressed other topics in different workshops, such as Israel's war against Gaza, the fight against ICE raids and the defense of immigrants, the demands for housing for the homeless, universal health care and the economic and political crisis of capitalism. It was conducted in a hybrid format, both in person and online (for people who were far away and willing to give their testimonies), with broad participation from all sectors of American society who maintain their discontent with the unpopular and neoliberal policies of the current US government. All of this also serves to plan further actions that unify organizations and movements in the current situation in the northern country, so that they can act against governmental irrationality and provide guarantees to the people for a better society. By Nuria Barbosa
